newsitem.title: JAPAN: Burger King says UK sales recover from "mad cow".
newsitem.headline: Burger King says UK sales recover from "mad cow".

text.p: Burger King Corp, the hamburger chain unit of Grand Metropolitan Plc, said on Thursday sales at its stores in Britain have recovered since being hit by the "mad cow" scare earlier this year.
"It (business) seems to have come back," Burger King Corp chief executive officer Robert Lowes told reporters in Tokyo. "We have been assuring our customers that we only use high-quality beef."

The possible link between Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), also known as "mad cow" disease, and Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD), its fatal human equivalent, turned off the appetites of hamburger-eaters in Germany and France as well, Lowes added.
Lowes said, however, that Burger King is now investigating the possibility of using a computer lineage tracing system, which would help sift out cows that have a history of the disease.
"We will be able to overwhelmingly reassure the consumer that the beef has nothing to do with the disease, by using such a system," Lowes said.
Grand Metropolitan Plc of Britain is the parent company of Burger King Corp, which is based in the United States.
